verdict.rationale: Terraform ships a native `terraform test` framework that runs against test-specific, short-lived resources, preventing any risk to existing infrastructure or state. Since v1.7.0 it can also mock provider data, so tests can run without real infrastructure, and `-json` output supports automation of test runs. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of the test framework, and deeper first-party detail on test authoring (assertions, run blocks).

support.subject: As a developer, I can write automated tests for my infrastructure code and run them without touching production

citations.quote: Tests run against test-specific, short-lived resources, preventing any risk to your existing infrastructure or state.
Terraform v1.7.0 introduced the ability to mock data returned by the providers during a `terraform test` execution.
For long-running commands such as `plan`, `apply`, `refresh`, and `test`, the `-json` flag outputs a stream of JSON UI messages.
